statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains deep below the block threshold during the CME weekend halt, with a narrow reopen window flagged for elevated gap sensitivity.
recommendation: Conditions are described as low Tail with moderate Stress. The single flagged window covers the 22:00-00:00 UTC Globex reopen, where weekend repricing would be expressed as a gap into thin liquidity. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail low after an orderly triple-witching close; hawkish Sunday Fed commentary lifts Stress into a narrow reopen window
body: This assessment is made during the CME weekend halt, so no live NQ price path is observable and none is asserted. The standing reference is Friday's close at 29,644.17 (+0.67%), struck in the upper part of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range on triple-witching expiry, with VIX easing to 14.81 (-4.08%). Cross-asset context is coherent rather than conflicting: the 10-year Treasury yield hovers near 5% and the 2-year sits at 4.67% after the FOMC raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 17 September, its first hike since 2023, while front-month WTI eased to about $100.30 in a third consecutive decline. The one materially new input since the prior assessment is hawkish weekend Fed commentary: Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is still too high across all aspects of the economy, and reporting the same day describes Wall Street positioning for further hikes with October odds above 50%. Under the applied risk definition this is narrative repricing, which raises Stress rather than the probability of a pathological no-retracement path. Tail therefore stays low: none of the conditions that define such a path - shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, NQ holding near extremes - can be observed while the venue is shut, and Friday's session ended in orderly fashion with split internals. Friday's tape showed strong semiconductor leadership (Semiconductor Equipment & Materials +4.85%, Semiconductors +1.87%) against a divided megacap complex and weaker Software, which argues for rotational two-way trade rather than aligned directional structure. Stress is moderate, reflecting the hawkish Fed repricing, elevated oil, and an active US-Iran tanker conflict in the Strait of Hormuz after the IRGC struck the Togo-flagged tanker Trend. Confidence is solid: current levels, yields, oil, volatility, verified weekend headlines and the forward calendar are all confirmed, yet no continuous price path exists to corroborate them and the shared cross-asset futures feed was unavailable this cycle. The single narrow danger window covers the Sunday reopen into thin liquidity.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe a stable, low-Tail regime. Tail held between 4% and 5% throughout, mapping to EA_ON and green in every hour, while Stress drifted up from 24% late on 19 September to a 31-33% band through the 16:00-18:00 UTC hours as hawkish Fed repricing and the elevated oil backdrop accumulated. Confidence ranged from 70% to 76%, easing late in the window as the weekend halt removed live price-path evidence. Dominant mode was recorded as normal in all 24 hours, and no interval showed the persistent one-way structure that would justify a higher Tail reading.
outlookSummary: The cycle spans the remainder of the CME weekend halt, the Sunday 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, the Asian and European sessions, and the Monday US cash session through 18:00 UTC. Tail is projected to stay in the low band throughout, peaking at 11% around the US cash open and at 9% at the reopen, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON in all 24 hours. The two structurally meaningful checkpoints are the reopen, where any weekend Fed or Hormuz repricing would arrive as a gap into thin liquidity, and the 13:30 UTC opening auction, which is the cycle's most reliable generator of genuine directional structure and the first session after Friday's triple-witching expiry. Monday carries only a Fed Goolsbee speech at 10:30 UTC and the second-tier Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30 UTC; the week's larger catalysts, flash PMIs on 23 September and the scheduled US-China summit later in the week, fall beyond this window. Apart from the current clock hour, no future price-path structure is treated as already observed.
